Definition: Extent to which the national digital identity system is integrated with the data exchange for identity verification and authentication
Comments: The e-Bêkou platform uses biometric logins. Over 300,000 civil status documents digitized in pilot phase with blockchain-backed registries. However, no national digital ID card or comprehensive biometric identity system integrated with a data exchange platform documented. Digital identity capabilities are being built within the e-government program.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Original harbingerstandard.com URL is dead, and its specific 'e-Bêkou' biometric-platform claim could not be corroborated anywhere — Bêkou is in fact an unrelated EU humanitarian trust fund, so this looks like a sourcing error. Independent evidence confirms the score on other grounds: the World Bank's Public Sector Digital Governance Project (effective Dec 2022) documents that digital ID verification/authentication is not yet possible in CAR, and the National Digital Identity System (SNID), announced Nov 2025 (USD13m budget), remains at feasibility/procurement stage with rollout planned for 2027-2032. Confirmed at 'Planned' (2).

Definition: Integration with national payment systems for government-to-person (G2P), government-to-business (G2B) transactions via data exchange
Comments: IFC/World Bank organized a workshop on digital financial services (November 2025) with 3 agreements signed between Ministry of Finance, Orange RCA, and Ecobank RCA. Mobile money used for some transactions. However, no integrated G2P government digital payments system with data exchange documented.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Cited acap-rca.org URL is dead (503 on repeated attempts), but the underlying event is corroborated elsewhere: an IFC-led workshop (10 Nov 2025) and three MoUs signed between the Ministry of Finance, Orange RCA and Ecobank RCA to accelerate digital financial services. These agreements concern general financial inclusion/mobile money, not a confirmed or even explicitly planned G2P/G2B government-payment integration via a data exchange platform. No evidence of that specific integration was found, so recalculated down to 'Not integrated' (1); flagged for human review given the ambiguity between broad DFS partnerships and this variable's narrower G2P/G2B data-exchange scope.

Definition: Extent to which the data exchange enables services accessible to all population groups including persons with disabilities, elderly, low literacy
Comments: Digital Points" with facilitators staffed to help residents create accounts and access services in some Bangui neighborhoods. Community radio campaigns and mobile network subsidies for data access planned. Solar-powered kiosks being tested for rural areas without devices. Partial accessibility improvements in progress.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Cited harbingerstandard.com page is dead, and its specific claims ('Digital Points' facilitators, solar kiosks) could not be corroborated by any other source. Independent evidence (FAO 2024/25 communications assessment; African Disability Rights Yearbook; Paradigm HQ digital-rights report) instead shows internet access at only around 10-12% of the population, concentrated in urban areas, no public services yet delivered digitally, and 'in practice, very little is done to ensure access for persons with disabilities.' This indicates accessibility is still limited rather than showing active improvements; recalculated down to 'Limited accessibility' (1).
